messages:
Priya (eng-platform): kicking off a heads-up — we rolled rate-policy v2 as a canary to 10% at 09:30 PT. Main change: reduced burst window and stricter token refill. Observability: please watch 429 spikes and queue latencies.

DeployBot: canary deployment event: rate-policy:v2 -> 10% traffic (region-us-west) at 2026-02-14T09:30Z. Commit: 97b1c4d.

Miguel (support): got a report from acme-corp facing increased 429s right after the canary. They pasted this response body: `{\"error\":\"tokens_exhausted\",\"detail\":\"burst quota exceeded\"}`.

Miguel (support): repro steps they shared: call pattern is lots of short-lived hot requests (10–20 reqs/sec) for ~40s, then idle. They say it worked before the canary.

Aisha (eng-sre): @Miguel can you drop a sample request-id and the upstream headers so I can trace the token-bucket metrics? Also which API key (masked) so we can match the customer rule.

Miguel (support): posted request-id: rq_8f3a2c9f, x-customer-id: acct-acme-42, x-api-key: sk-***. Pasting a stripped curl they used:

```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -H 'X-Customer-ID: acct-acme-42' \
  -d '{\"prompt\":\"short request\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Aisha (eng-sre): traced rq_8f3a2c9f — runtime shows token-bucket drop to 0 after ~18s and subsequent requests returned 429. Logs snippet: 

```
[2026-02-14T09:31:12Z] rq_8f3a2c9f INFO token_bucket: consumer=acct-acme-42 bucket=0 refill_rate=5/s window=5s
[2026-02-14T09:31:13Z] rq_8f3a2c9f WARN rate_limiter: deny 429 reason=tokens_exhausted policy=rate-policy:v2
```

Tom (eng-runtime): that matches the change we pushed: burst_window default dropped from 20s -> 5s in v2. Intended to reduce long tail cost, but it's harsher for short bursts where customers rely on longer refill amortization.

Tom (eng-runtime): options: 
- rollback the canary entirely to v1 for the 10% cohort, or
- patch targeted exceptions for known Dedicated accounts (whitelist burst window), or
- relax v2 parameters (increase burst_window or refill_rate) and re-deploy.

Priya (eng-platform): product asks for minimal customer impact. For high-value Dedicated accounts like Acme we should prefer targeted rollback/exception. Full canary rollback is heavier and affects rollout telemetry. Thoughts?

Nora (customer-success): Acme is on an annual contract and is highly sensitive. They need immediate fix. They reported timeouts that impact their SLA. CS requests a targeted rollback or temporary whitelist for acct-acme-42.

Aisha (eng-sre): tactical plan to target rollback: patch cluster configmap 'rate-policies' to remove acct-acme-42 from canary_targets and add a temporary override rule for their API key. Steps below. I'll run the change once we agree.

```
# remove acct-acme-42 from canary and add override rule
kubectl -n infra patch configmap rate-policies --type=json -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/data/canary_targets/acct-acme-42"}]'
# add override (lower priority, temporary)
kubectl -n infra patch configmap rate-policies --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/data/overrides/acct-acme-42","value":"{\"burst_window\":20,\"refill_rate\":10}"}]'
```

Tom (eng-runtime): after configmap patch I'll trigger a runtime reload on the pool that serves Dedicated keys: `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/rr-runtime` (region-us-west). Expect ~30s to pick up config.

Miguel (support): will notify Acme that we're applying a fix and will follow up when changes complete. Also requests a regression test to confirm 429s stop.

Priya (eng-platform): agree — targeted rollback + override. Aisha you run the configmap patch now. Tom will handle runtime reload. Miguel/Nora will coordinate customer comms. Post-change we'll execute the repro script 3x over 60s to confirm.

Aisha (eng-sre): applying patch now. Pushing commit to infra-config: 3f9d2a1.

DeployBot: configmap patch accepted, commit 3f9d2a1, pipeline started.

Tom (eng-runtime): rolling runtime restart on region-us-west pools now. Monitoring logs for reload.

[~1m pass]

Aisha (eng-sre): reload complete. Runtime picked up override for acct-acme-42.

Miguel (support): ran repro script against acct-acme-42 (same curl pattern) 3x over 60s — no 429s observed. Latency stable. Confirmed with customer on call — they report normal behavior now. :thumbsup:

Priya (eng-platform): :tada: Great. Next: we should add a guard to the rollout process — for Dedicated accounts, default to preserve burst_window unless explicitly opted into v2. Action items:
- Tom: change rollout gating to exclude Dedicated keys (runtime change)
- Aisha: add alert rule for sudden 429% jumps post-canary (immediate)
- Miguel/Nora: document repro and customer timeline for postmortem

Tom (eng-runtime): noted. I'll open a PR to change gating and add a soft-fail if high-value accounts would be impacted.

Aisha (eng-sre): I'll create an incident card with link to logs and the commands used. Will add runbook steps we executed (patch, restart, verify).

Miguel (support): will draft a short customer note and update the ticket.

Priya (eng-platform): thanks team. We'll keep the canary for other customers but with stricter monitoring and a quick targeting rollback path. Follow-up: postmortem + decide whether v2 params need tuning before broader rollout.

DeployBot: pipeline completed, config live for region-us-west.

Nora (customer-success): customer is off the call and satisfied for now. Please loop me into the postmortem.

Priya (eng-platform): will schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to review telemetry and decide on next steps. Closing thread for now.

-- end of thread --
